result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_number_si()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values with SI (metric) prefixes. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L586-L724){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_number_si( x, unit=None, decimals=2, n_sigfig=None, drop_trailing_zeros=False, drop_trailing_dec_mark=True, scale_by=1, prefix_mode="engineering", pattern="{x}", sep_mark=",", dec_mark=".", force_sign=False, incl_space=True, locale=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Format numeric values with SI (International System of Units) prefixes, automatically selecting the appropriate prefix to keep the mantissa in a readable range. SI prefixes range from quetta (Q, 10^30) to quecto (q, 10^-30) and are commonly used in scientific and engineering contexts to represent very large or very small quantities with units (e.g., `"5.2 kW"`, `"3.8 ng"`, `"1.2 GHz"`, etc.). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [unit]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A character string specifying the unit to append after the SI prefix (e.g., `"g"` for grams, `"W"` for watts, `"Hz"` for hertz, `"m"` for meters). If `None`, only the prefix will be shown. [decimals]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[2]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The `decimals` values corresponds to the exact number of decimal places to use. A value such as `2.34` can, for example, be formatted with `0` decimal places and it would result in `"2"`. With `4` decimal places, the formatted value becomes `"2.3400"`. The trailing zeros can be removed with `drop_trailing_zeros=True`. If `n_sigfig` is provided, `decimals` is ignored. [n_sigfig]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A option to format numbers to *n* significant figures. By default, this is `None` and thus number values will be formatted according to the number of decimal places set via `decimals=`. If opting to format according to the rules of significant figures, `n_sigfig=` must be a number greater than or equal to `1`. Any values passed to the `decimals=` and `drop_trailing_zeros=` arguments will be ignored. [drop_trailing_zeros]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A boolean value that allows for removal of trailing zeros (those redundant zeros after the decimal mark). [drop_trailing_dec_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A boolean value that determines whether decimal marks should always appear even if there are no decimal digits to display after formatting (e.g., `23` becomes `23.` if `False`). By default trailing decimal marks are not shown. [scale_by]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : All numeric values will be multiplied by the `scale_by` value before undergoing formatting. Since the `default` value is `1`, no values will be changed unless a different multiplier value is supplied. This is useful for unit conversions (e.g., converting metric tons to grams by using `scale_by=1_000_000`). [prefix_mode]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["engineering"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The type of SI prefixes to use. Use `"engineering"` (the default) for prefixes that correspond to powers of 1000 only. Use `"decimal"` to include all SI prefixes (also those for powers of 10 and 100). [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` (which can be used multiple times, if needed) and all other characters will be interpreted as string literals. [sep_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[","]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The string to use as a separator between groups of digits. [dec_mark]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["."]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The string to be used as the decimal mark. [force_sign]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Should the positive sign be shown for positive values (effectively showing a sign for all values except zero)? If so, use `True` for this option. [incl_space]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : An option for whether to include a space between the numerical value and the SI prefix + unit (e.g., `True` for `"1.5 kW"`, `False` for `"1.5kW"`). Per SI convention, there should be a space between the value and the unit symbol. The default is `True`. [locale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional locale identifier that can be used for formatting values according the locale's rules. Examples include `"en"` for English (United States) and `"fr"` for French (France). When provided, overrides `sep_mark` and `dec_mark` with locale-appropriate values. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Let's format a vector of numeric values with SI prefixes. ::: {#8e64aab4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_number_si([1.5e9, 2.7e6, 4200, 0.3, 0.00012, 2.4e-8]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['1.50 G', '2.70 M', '4.20 k', '300.00 m', '120.00 µ', '24.00 n'] ``` ::: ::: We can add a unit designation to show what the values represent (e.g., watts). ::: {#8539c247 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} vals.fmt_number_si([1.5e9, 2.7e6, 4200], unit="W") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['1.50 GW', '2.70 MW', '4.20 kW'] ``` ::: ::: The `scale_by` option is useful for unit conversions. For instance, to convert metric tons to grams before formatting: ::: {#46231da3 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} vals.fmt_number_si([455, 331, 235, 30], unit="g", scale_by=1_000_000, decimals=0) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` ['455 Mg', '331 Mg', '235 Mg', '30 Mg'] ``` ::: ::: We can control the space between the number and unit with `incl_space`. ::: {#cc74c28d .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} vals.fmt_number_si([2.4e9, 5.0e9, 900e6], unit="Hz", incl_space=False, decimals=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['2.4GHz', '5.0GHz', '900.0MHz'] ``` ::: :::
